correctness.rationale: For n≥8 triangle-free simple G with pairwise edge-disjoint four-cycles, dual K of ordinary Δ3 has complete one-skeleton, triangles exactly 2-edge paths (T=Σ_v binom(d(v),2)), tetrahedra exactly the q square vertex sets, and no 4-simplices (all 10 triples in 5-set connected would give at least 7 edges on a triangle-free 5-set, contradicting Turán extremum 6). Every path triangle outside a square has unique common neighbor endpoint and a private free nonedge. For a cyclic square a,b,c,d, collapse tetrahedron along abd, bcd along bd, abc along bc, acd along ac; the square-edge and diagonal freedom survives across distinct squares because 4-cycles are edge-disjoint. The resulting connected graph deletes T−q one-skeleton edges and has cycle rank B=binom(n−1,2)−T+q≥0. Integral Alexander duality gives sole top free homology; complete (n−6)-skeleton plus Hurewicz/Whitehead upgrades to wedge B S^{n−4}; disconnected components allowed. Four-cycle count counts edge-sets once, not orientations.
residual_risks: A representative verify.py is not an exhaustive classification of arbitrarily large edge-disjoint-square graphs.
No claim for overlapping square edges, triangles, or shellability.
